verses.english: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

verses.pali: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme asurā jiniṁsu, devā parājiniṁsu.
verses.english: In that battle the titans won and the gods lost.

verses.pali: Parājitā ca kho, bhikkhave, devā apāyaṁsveva uttarenamukhā, abhiyaṁsveva ne asurā.
verses.english: Defeated, the gods fled north with the titans in pursuit.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātali saṅgāhakaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed his chariot handler Mātali in verse:
in the Red Silk-Cotton Woods with your draft-pole.
I’d rather give up our lives to the titans
than deprive these birds of their nests.’

verses.pali: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā sahassayuttaṁ ājaññarathaṁ paccudāvattesi.
verses.english: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Mātali. And he turned the chariot back around, with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds.

verses.pali: ‘paccudāvatto kho dāni sakkassa devānamindassa sahassayutto ājaññaratho.
Dutiyampi kho devā asurehi saṅgāmessantī’ti bhītā asurapurameva pāvisiṁsu.
verses.english: The titans will have to fight the gods a second time!’ Terrified, they retreated right away to the citadel of the titans.

verses.pali: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa dhammena jayo ahosī”ti.
verses.english: And that’s how Sakka came to win victory by principle.”
